props.title: Spanish guitar for private events, played by Dirty Flamenco.
props.lede: The plates are cleared, Gary Meyers leans into a bulería, the cajón answers him, and the whole table turns to watch. Dirty Flamenco is a working flamenco trio of guitar, bass and cajón. It plays under the conversation through cocktails and dinner, then steps forward for one set piece where your evening has space for it.

items.q: Is Dirty Flamenco traditional flamenco or Spanish guitar?
items.a: Traditional flamenco. The repertoire is palos, the traditional forms: bulerias, solea, alegrias and tangos. A Spanish guitar booking plays familiar songs with a Spanish flavor; a flamenco booking plays the forms themselves. Dirty Flamenco is fronted by Gary Meyers and booked through Signet Artists in Denver.

Under dinner it plays at the level of the conversation, so the table talks across it. The set piece is louder on purpose, because it's the part everyone stops to watch. The trio sets the level to the space and the crowd, and if your venue has a sound limit, just let us know the number and the trio plays under it.

items.q: Is Spanish guitar right for a wedding ceremony?
items.a: Yes. Nylon strings carry a processional and a recessional without amplification in most spaces, and the repertoire moves between Spanish pieces and the songs a couple asks for.
Yes. With a dancer the trio becomes a quartet, and the dancer is the set piece. Just let us know and we'll price the quartet with the date.
